chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Fuzayl who said:

A slave on loan said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I said to my master, 'Sell me for seven hundred Dirhams and I shall give you three hundred Dirhams'. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'If it was that there was wealth for you on the day you stipulated, so it would be upon you that you give it, and if there did not happen to be any wealth for you on that day, so there is nothing upon you'.

key_terms.غُلَامٌ سِنْدِيٌّ: A slave on loan or hired slave
key_terms.فَعَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُعْطِيَهُ: So it is upon you to give it

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a slave to be obligated to pay his master for his freedom in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the obligation of the agreed manumission price is contingent upon the slave's financial status at the precise moment the contract was concluded, rather than their current ability to pay. This ruling highlights the principle of fairness in Islamic jurisprudence, ensuring that a slave is not burdened with a debt they could not have reasonably fulfilled when the agreement was struck. It underscores the merciful nature of the master-slave relationship in Shia fiqh, where the condition is binding only if the prerequisite of wealth existed at the time of stipulation.
